content:
A lot of businesses in Gurugram run on spreadsheets that have grown too big. A real estate sales team tracks site visits in a shared Excel file. A logistics firm near Manesar dispatches trucks from WhatsApp groups. A coaching institute reconciles fee payments by hand every month. None of this is wrong at the start, but at some point the workarounds cost more than a proper system would. That is the point where custom software makes sense, and it is the work we do at TopWebExpert.

This page explains what custom software development in Gurugram looks like with us: the kinds of systems we build, how a project runs, how your data is protected, and what you get at the end.

Signs You Have Outgrown Off-the-Shelf Tools

  • Staff copy the same data between two or three tools every day.
  • You pay for a SaaS product but use a small part of it, and the part you need is missing.
  • Reports take someone a full day to put together at the end of each month.
  • Only one person understands how the current spreadsheet works.
  • Customers or vendors keep asking for status updates you cannot give quickly.

If only one of these applies, a better-configured existing tool may be enough. If several apply, a custom system usually pays for itself in saved time and fewer errors.

What We Build

Most of our software projects fall into a few categories:

  • CRM and lead management
  • ERP modules and inventory
  • Booking and scheduling systems
  • Customer and vendor portals
  • Internal dashboards and reporting
  • Field-force and dispatch tools
  • SaaS products for startups
  • API integrations between existing systems

Typical examples: a broker portal for a developer selling projects along Dwarka Expressway, a patient-records and billing module for a multi-specialty clinic, or a subscription back office for a D2C brand that needs Razorpay, courier aggregator APIs and GST invoices in one place.

The Technology Underneath

We choose proven, widely used tools so that any competent developer can maintain your system later, including your own hires:

  • Backend: Laravel (PHP) or Node.js, with Python where data processing is involved.
  • Frontend: React or Vue for web dashboards and portals.
  • Database: MySQL or PostgreSQL, with Redis for caching and queues.
  • Hosting: AWS, DigitalOcean or your existing servers, with automated backups.
  • Integrations: UPI and card payments, WhatsApp Business API, SMS gateways, Tally or Zoho exports, Google Workspace.

How a Project Runs

We split every project into phases, each with a clear output you can review:

  1. Discovery workshop (1–2 weeks). We sit with the people who will use the system, map the current process step by step, and list what must change. Our office is on Sohna Road in Sector 49, so teams from Udyog Vihar, MG Road or Golf Course Extension Road can come in for a working session, or we come to you.
  2. Specification and prototype (1–2 weeks). A written scope, a data model and clickable screens. You sign off before development starts, and the fixed quote is based on this document.
  3. Development in sprints (6–16 weeks). Two-week cycles, each ending with a demo on a staging server your team can log in to.
  4. Data migration and user acceptance testing (2–3 weeks). We import your existing records, your team tests with real cases, and we fix what they find.
  5. Go-live and training (1 week). Launch, hands-on training sessions and written guides for each user role.

A small internal tool can be done in about two months. A multi-module system with several integrations can take four to six months. We would rather phase a large project than rush it.

Your Data and the DPDP Act

If your software stores customer or employee information, the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 applies to you as a data fiduciary. We build with that in mind: role-based access so staff see only what they need, audit logs of who changed what, encrypted connections, consent records where personal data is collected, and a practical way to find and delete a person's data on request. We also keep test and development environments free of real personal data.

Ownership, Handover and Support

You own everything we build for you once it is paid for: source code, database, documentation and designs. The code sits in a Git repository under your account from day one, not ours. At handover you get server credentials, a technical guide for future developers and an admin guide for your team. After a post-launch warranty period for bug fixes, you can choose a monthly support plan or take maintenance in-house.

How We Keep Quality Up

  • Peer code review on every change before it is merged.
  • Automated tests for business rules such as pricing, commissions and tax calculations.
  • A separate staging server that mirrors production.
  • Security checks against common web risks such as SQL injection and broken access control.
  • Load testing when the system will serve many users at once.

Where Custom Software Projects Go Wrong

We see the same problems again and again when clients come to us after a failed attempt elsewhere. The biggest is skipping discovery and letting developers guess the process. The second is designing only for management reports and forgetting the staff who enter the data every day. Others include having no one on the client side who owns the project, leaving data migration to the last week, and accepting a system without documentation.

Who This Is Not For

Custom software is not the right choice if a standard tool like Zoho, Tally or a well-known CRM already covers most of what you need and your team is happy with it. It is also not a fit if you need a full system in three weeks, or if nobody in your business can give time to explain processes and test the software. In those cases we will point you to a simpler route.

Frequently Asked Questions

How do you price a custom software project?

Price depends on the number of modules and user roles, integrations, data migration and how complex your business rules are. We do not quote before understanding the process. After a free consultation and discovery, you get a fixed quote tied to a written scope.

Can the software connect with Tally or our existing tools?

Usually yes. Most tools offer an API or an import and export route. We check this during discovery and confirm what is possible before quoting.

Can we start with one module and add more later?

Yes, and we often recommend it. Starting with the module that removes the most manual work lets your team adapt before the next phase.

What if our developer leaves after handover?

Because we use common frameworks and hand over documentation and the full repository, any experienced Laravel, Node.js or React developer can pick up the code.

Do you work with companies outside Gurugram?

Yes. Our base is in Gurugram (many people still search for us as a Gurgaon agency), but discovery and reviews work well over video calls for clients elsewhere.
